text: {"summary":"A lanky street interviewer approaches a random heavyset man and asks what he would do after winning the five-number lottery jackpot. The interviewer suggests conventional luxuries and repeatedly blurts out “pina,” while the man explains that he would buy an enormous box packed with ten-millimetre open-end wrenches and scatter them everywhere. The absurd escalation ends with the man imagining that every time he reaches for a six-millimetre bolt, there will be not one but five wrenches available, while physically trampling the interviewer.","characters":[{"name":"skinny interviewer with microphone","description":"A lanky, energetic, wide-eyed man conducting a street interview with a handheld microphone. He speaks in an excited, rapid-fire, colloquial register, offers guesses as prompts, and repeatedly shouts the vulgar word “pinák?” as if it were an obvious lottery priority."},{"name":"heavyset bald respondent","description":"A large, bald, heavyset man in a hooded sweatshirt who is stopped for the interview. He begins hesitantly, then answers in increasingly emphatic, vulgar everyday speech, using “bazmeg” and “vágod?” as forceful conversational punctuation."}],"panels":[{"panelId":"p0","description":"The skinny interviewer with microphone announces excitedly that they will wait for the first random Tibor and ask him the question. The large speech bubble belongs to him; r1 contains no readable speech."},{"panelId":"p1","description":"The skinny interviewer with microphone greets the heavyset bald respondent and asks what he would do first if he won the five-number lottery jackpot. The long bubble tail points back to the interviewer."},{"panelId":"p2","description":"The interviewer rapidly suggests a sports car, yacht, travel, villa, and “pinák?” as possible answers. The respondent’s separate bubble says he is considering the lottery win and then answers “igen!”; the repeated “pinák?” interruptions are the interviewer’s."},{"panelId":"p3","description":"The respondent begins his actual answer while the interviewer holds the microphone toward him. The respondent says he would buy a huge box filled to the brim with ten-millimetre open-end wrenches; the empty boxed regions contain no speech."},{"panelId":"p4","description":"The respondent continues describing the plan, saying he would scatter the wrenches everywhere like a dandelion scattering its seeds. The bubble tail points to the heavyset respondent on the right, not to the interviewer."},{"panelId":"p5","description":"The respondent’s explanation is visualized as an absurd giant toothed mouth swallowing a person holding a wrench, with the microphone dropped on the ground. The text is still the respondent’s speech: whenever there is a six-millimetre bolt, damn it, there should be a wrench."},{"panelId":"p6","description":"The heavyset respondent stands over the flattened interviewer and delivers the final clarification: wherever he reaches, there should be five wrenches, not one. The interviewer and microphone lie on the ground, turning the verbal absurdity into slapstick."}],"speakers":{"r0":"skinny interviewer with microphone","r1":"none","r2":"skinny interviewer with microphone","r3":"skinny interviewer with microphone","r4":"skinny interviewer with microphone","r5":"heavyset bald respondent","r6":"skinny interviewer with microphone","r7":"skinny interviewer with microphone","r8":"skinny interviewer with microphone","r9":"none","r10":"skinny interviewer with microphone","r11":"skinny interviewer with microphone","r12":"none","r13":"heavyset bald respondent","r14":"none","r15":"heavyset bald respondent","r16":"heavyset bald respondent","r17":"heavyset bald respondent"},"notes":["“Randomtibor” means an arbitrary, generic man named Tibor; Tibor is a common Hungarian male first name, so the phrase evokes a random ordinary passer-by rather than a specific person.","“Lottó ötös” literally means the lottery five, referring to Hungary’s five-number lottery jackpot. It should be localized as winning the five-number lottery or jackpot, not as five lottery tickets.","“Pinák” is the vulgar plural of “pina,” literally referring to vaginas/pussies. The interviewer keeps proposing sex or women as the obvious first purchase after winning the lottery; the repetition is the running gag and should remain blunt rather than being softened.","The respondent’s “kurvanagy” is an intensifier meaning “fucking huge” or “damn huge.” It is written as one compound word in Hungarian and conveys rough, emphatic speech.","“Tizes villáskulcs” means a size-ten open-end wrench, conventionally a 10 mm wrench. The comedy depends on the mundane specificity of buying thousands of ordinary tools instead of luxury goods.","“Telis-tele ... agyig rakva” means packed completely full, literally up to the top/brain level. The answer is deliberately overexplained and obsessively practical.","“Pitypang a szarjait” compares scattering the wrenches to a dandelion scattering its seeds, but calls the seeds its “shits.” “Szar” is a vulgar word for feces and, by extension, “crap”; preserve the crude biological image.","“Vágod?” literally means “Are you cutting it?” but is colloquial Hungarian for “Do you get it?” or “You know what I mean?” It marks the respondent as casual and emphatic, not genuinely as asking about cutting.","“Bazmeg” is a highly vulgar Hungarian swear/interjection, literally related to “fuck me,” used broadly like “fuck,” “for fuck’s sake,” or “damn it.” It appears in r16 and r17 and should remain strong profanity.","The clipped or fused greetings “JÓESTÉT” and “JÓNAPOT” are informal/nonstandard renderings of “jó estét” and “jó napot” (“good evening” and “good day”). They help make the interviewer’s street-interview voice brisk and unpolished; do not normalize the comic’s deliberate spelling in a reference translation unless the target language has an equivalent roughness.","The interviewer’s guesses in r3, r4, r6, r7, r8, r10, and r11 create a rhythm of conventional lottery fantasies interrupted by the repeated “PINÁK?” The respondent’s delayed, mundane wrench obsession is the punchline to those expectations.","The six-millimetre bolt in r16 is contrasted with the ten-millimetre wrenches in r13. The mismatch is part of the absurdity: the respondent wants an enormous supply of vaguely relevant tools everywhere, not a sensible toolkit.","The final “NEM EGY, ÖT!” means “Not one, five!” It exaggerates the already ridiculous plan and explains the physical gag: the respondent wants multiple wrenches available at every possible reach.","There are no readable background signs, labels, vehicle names, or changing signs in any panel. No sign text needs to be recreated or explained."}]}

json.name: skinny interviewer with microphone
json.description: A lanky, energetic, wide-eyed man conducting a street interview with a handheld microphone. He speaks in an excited, rapid-fire, colloquial register, offers guesses as prompts, and repeatedly shouts the vulgar word “pinák?” as if it were an obvious lottery priority.
